## Intended repository tree

```text
scgsim/
├── README.md                 # SCGSim Development-owned package entry
├── _quarto.yml               # SCGSim Development-owned site configuration
├── _extensions/              # SCGSim Development-owned vendored Quarto extensions
├── docs/                     # SCGSim Development-owned authored Quarto sources/assets
├── src/scgsim/               # SCGSim Development-owned product source
├── scripts/                  # SCGSim Development-owned producers/tooling
└── tests/                    # SCGSim Development-owned stabilization tests
```

Generated site output is never source authority.

## Responsibility map

| Owner | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| SCGSim Development | Package/build/runtime/report source, schemas, tests, scripts, CI/release, README, Quarto site configuration and extensions, authored documentation and assets, information architecture and prose, generated-reference placement/presentation |
| OrPen SC PDK | Public PDK facts, public Component source, and public component-simulation notebooks |
| Chip Design EPR | Surface-EPR requirements and private consumer validation only |
| `scq-ansys-aedt` | Version-locked AEDT/PyAEDT procedure only; no repository path ownership |
| Integration & Sync | Repository settings, merges, future pins, synchronization, and cleanup |

Generated API reference may be produced from product-owned source, while its
placement and presentation remain package-owned. No owner listed here may
infer Human acceptance, publication authority, or merge authority from a green
build.

## Public documentation site

The canonical site is `https://orpenstrike.github.io/scgsim/`. Stable `main`
carries the latest stable release; `develop` carries the next prerelease line.
Native Askr presentation is confirmed and the 1.0.1 maintenance release is
authorized. Instructional content revisions remain a separate scope; runtime
V1 and existing ownership boundaries remain stabilized.

The site has four Areas: Overview, Tutorial, Concept and Contract. Every
Area has a floating **Pages** menu; the right **Sections** TOC stays within the
current document. Contract groups public
contracts, implementation/ownership/provenance, and project history. Each page
keeps one editable Markdown or Quarto authority and its existing URL.

### Source and presentation ownership

SCGSim vendors the complete unmodified upstream `_extensions/askr` from
[Askr v0.4.1](https://github.com/arfiligol/askr/tree/4255c04004fafb34de72a625f419b9ae4a837ac1)
at commit `4255c04004fafb34de72a625f419b9ae4a837ac1` under
`_extensions/arfiligol/askr`. SCGSim uses native Askr presentation without a consumer stylesheet or explicit
reader-mode activation. `_quarto.yml` supplies site identity, authored navigation
and execution settings; the upstream extension remains unmodified. Quarto
1.10.18 is the rendering toolchain.

`scripts/pages_versions.json` is the editable version catalogue. The builder
resolves and freezes actual source commits and package metadata. It renders
development, current stable and pinned historical versions separately, with
branch-local search and one atomic publication. When the current stable
version also appears in pinned history, those entries coalesce into one site.
Version roots include `/scgsim/v1.0.0/`, `/scgsim/v1.0.1/`, and the
development root `/scgsim/v1.0.1-dev/`.

The root selects the latest stable version. Legacy `/main/` and `/develop/`
aliases preserve the requested page, query and fragment when routing to their
selected version. When switching versions, a page absent from the destination falls back to
that version's home. An unknown requested path still reports absence through
the static host, rather than a fabricated successful page. The inline Askr version catalogue is the same across all
sites, and a version change keeps the current page where that version has it.

Current main and develop use their own content and configuration. Historical
1.0.0 preserves its exact original README and Quarto bodies while using the
reviewed presentation overlay: website/format configuration and the exact
Askr pin. View source points to the original content revision.
The footer and `build.json` distinguish package version, content SHA,
presentation SHA, Askr commit and source branch. Generated HTML, search indexes
and version manifests are derived artifacts, never a second editable source.

### Publication and diagnostics

The **Documentation Pages** workflow owns publication. Pushes to `develop` or
`main`, and manual `workflow_dispatch`, start the combined build. At build
start it captures source identities for the available branches and pinned
history, renders clean tracked snapshots with code execution disabled, then
publishes one artifact. Pull requests do not publish. Source changes reach
stable main through the reviewed develop-to-main promotion process; stable
metadata belongs to main, not the published develop branch.

If any required version render fails, publication must not run and the last
successful deployment remains. Inspect the failing Actions run and build logs,
correct the tracked source/configuration and use the same workflow. For a
one-off rebuild without source changes, open **Actions → Documentation Pages →
Run workflow** and select the published branch. Deployment failures belong to
the deploy job and `github-pages` environment; repository Pages settings and
synchronization remain Integration & Sync responsibilities.

For a local diagnostic build, use Python 3.12 and Quarto 1.10.18. The existing
`--output` interface names a new directory:

```bash
preview_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
rmdir "$preview_dir"
python scripts/build_docs_site.py --output "$preview_dir"
```

A normal build uses captured published refs. A prepublication preview may use
explicit clean exported candidate sources supported by the builder; it records
that supplied content identity and does not claim the remote already contains
it. Keep the candidate export, original content identity and presentation
overlay distinct. Local output is not uploaded by hand, and publication does
not use a Pages branch or personal access token.
